learning_outcomes.text: Understand the fundamentals and basic applications of thermal machines and engines, knowing how to apply them to practical situations in industry and other economic sectors, with quality, safety, effectiveness, and judgment, using the minimum possible resources.
Understand and know how to take the necessary measures to minimize the environmental impact of thermal machines and engines.
Understand, master, and apply all concepts related to thermal machines and engines to improve their operation and lay the groundwork for future innovations.

Solve problems and practical situations concerning various industrial power processes, steam generation, and others related to thermal machines and engines, and their adaptation to the most common real situations.

Be able to apply the optimal use and deployment of thermal machines and engines to various situations, equipment, systems, and processes they will encounter in their professional life, both in industry and other sectors (residential, services, transport, etc.), using minimal resources and seeking intelligent and innovative solutions, leading the process and the search for solutions, minimizing their effects on the environment.
Acquire the foundations for multidisciplinary participation with criteria of leadership, quality design, intelligent teamwork, problem-solving with innovative bases, seeking oriented solutions.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1: Introduction to Thermal Machines and Engines - The thermal machine - The thermal engine - The direct Carnot cycle - The inverse Carnot cycle

Topic 2: Steam Turbines - Introduction - Classification of steam turbines - Stages of the steam turbine - Multiple or multi-stage turbine - Losses in pipes - Internal efficiency of a stage - Internal efficiency of the pipe. Recovery factor - Effective efficiency and power of a turboset - Relationship between power and steam consumption

Topic 3: Steam Boilers - Introduction - Energy balance in a control volume with chemical reactions - Types of steam generators - Mass, energy, and exergy balances in a boiler - Efficiency of a steam boiler - Energy saving in boilers

Topic 4: Steam Thermal Power Plants - The Rankine cycle - Internal irreversibilities in the Rankine cycle - Rankine cycle improvements - Thermodynamic analysis of a regenerative cycle - Thermodynamic analysis of a thermal power plant

Topic 5: Gas Turbines - Introduction - Internal combustion and external combustion gas turbines - Brayton cycle - Brayton cycle with internal irreversibilities - Other gas turbine cycles - Industrial gas turbines - Combined cycle plants - External combustion gas turbine

Topic 6: Reciprocating Internal Combustion Engines - Introduction - Classification - Operating cycle of an SI engine - Operating cycle of a CI engine - Standard air cycles - Effective power of an ICE - Characteristic curves - Supercharging

Topic 7: Cogeneration - Introduction - Generation and cogeneration - Topping cycles and bottoming cycles - Cogeneration technologies - Cogeneration in residential and tertiary sectors - Efficiency criteria for cogeneration plants - The effect of irreversibilities in a cogeneration plant - Advantages and disadvantages of cogeneration - Factors contributing to fostering cogeneration - Environmental impact of cogeneration plants

Practical Work - Solving problems of Thermal Machines and Engines using EES software - Implementation of Cogeneration Systems in the Residential Sector - Tutored work on practical applications of Thermal Machines and Engines
assessment_rules: A minimum of 35% of the total score in written exams is required. Failure to meet this criterion results in a maximum course grade of 4.5 (FAIL), even if the sum of all components is higher. Written exams (60%) are recoverable. Other assessment components (oral exams, lab reports, works and projects totaling 40%) are not recoverable, except for part-time students who may replace them with equivalent alternative assessments.
